messages:
morgan: Quick q — I'm baking a CI job that calls the Redwood CLI from a container and I want it to also be ergonomic for local devs on mac/linux/windows. What's the recommended pattern for storing profiles/auth for scripts? keyring + env fallback? any gotchas with non-interactive login or streaming?

eli: For CI we usually go env-first. Set REDWOOD_TOKEN (or REDWOOD_API_KEY) in the CI secret store and use `--token`/`--non-interactive` when available. Avoid keyring in containers.

samir: Agree. Dev setup: we rely on XDG config + keyring on mac/linux and credential manager on Windows. But add an explicit `--profile` arg so CI and dev profiles are isolated.

morgan: Example for the CI container would be super helpful — particularly for scripting output (parsing success/failure) and ensuring no TTY prompts.

eli: Example snippet we use in pipelines:```bash
export REDWOOD_TOKEN="${REDWOOD_TOKEN}"
redwood auth login --token "${REDWOOD_TOKEN}" --profile ci --non-interactive --output json
# then calls use `--profile ci`
redwood request --profile ci --output json "/models/list"
```
The `--output json` is important so your script can parse errors vs results.

sophia: Small note for Windows devs: some versions of the CLI default to Windows Credential Manager and will try to show a GUI prompt on first access. For dev ergonomics add `--no-keyring` or set `REDWOOD_NO_KEYRING=1` in powershell scripts to force env/profile file.

jamal: If you need long-lived profiles copied around in dotfiles, prefer symlinking a single `~/.config/redwood/profiles` file rather than copying token files. That avoids accidental duplication and stale tokens.

morgan: Nice. Any advice on token rotation? CI needs to gracefully refresh without human intervention.

samir: We issue short-lived tokens for CI and use a small refresh helper that runs as a step: it calls your auth provider and writes new token to a profile file or exports to env for the rest of the job. Keep it idempotent. Example:```bash
# pseudo: fetch token from vault or oidc
TOKEN=$(vault write -field=token auth/oidc/login role=ci)
export REDWOOD_TOKEN="${TOKEN}"
redwood auth login --token "${TOKEN}" --profile ci --non-interactive --output json
```
Also fail the job fast if `redwood request` returns 401 so rotation step can be retried.

eli: Streaming gotcha: in non-interactive shells, streaming works but buffering may hide tokens or errors in some shells. Use `--output json` for control-plane calls and `--stream` only for user-facing dev commands. In CI prefer non-streaming.

morgan: Great, this helps. I'll standardize our setup: CI uses env token + `--profile ci --non-interactive --output json`; devs default to keyring unless they set `REDWOOD_NO_KEYRING=1`. I'll post the example pipeline snippet in the repo. Thanks! :thumbsup:

devex-bot: FYI — internal doc link: https://redwood.devex/internal/cli-auth-patterns (added to #devex resources).
